questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift to neutral first.
Accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, move down one gear at a time. Slowly release the clutch between each downshift.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver sees you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of the lane so you appear in the driver's rearview mirror where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: The best way to brake in a straight line is to:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance on a straight road. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back on the seat so your arms stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not support your weight. Your arms should bend slightly at the grips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly. Release the throttle and go straight. If you must brake, use only the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be operated in curves.
Should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: Studies show that motorcycles with headlights on during the day:

options.text: Are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
Are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
Confuse other drivers.
Are less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers during the day.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a clear view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and lets them see you. Avoid staying in another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop other drivers from passing you.
Travel to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your lane and tells other drivers what you intend to do.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After riding for at least one hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcyclist should tell the passenger to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on after the engine has started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after the engine has started.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before riding. Tell them to get on only after you start the engine. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt. Their feet must stay on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake softer than usual to avoid overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight. Your motorcycle will need extra space to stop completely. Plan ahead and start slowing earlier.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Use low heels that won't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: May help other drivers see you.
Can be distracting.
Don't improve a rider's visibility.
Are not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: May help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a brightly-colored helmet. It protects you in a crash and helps other road users see you.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: Acceleration is faster, but stopping takes longer.
Both acceleration and stopping take longer.
Acceleration is slower, but stopping is faster.
Both acceleration and stopping are faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both acceleration and stopping take longer.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo slows acceleration and increases stopping distance.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs show road rules that riders must follow.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the road.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to get split up.
The group reaches the destination faster than a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: The group reaches the destination faster than a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better because it uses less road space, is easier to see, and stays together at traffic lights. Speed is not affected by how close together riders are.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what could happen?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may sound.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light may turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while moving too fast, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting into a lower gear.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Skip using turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Look only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: Which item will protect your eyes from the wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect a rider's eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of turn signals. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Is less effective than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent monotony.
Choose a lane position that maximizes their space cushion.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that maximizes their space cushion.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.
